questions_and_answers.question: What is omitted in a special conditional clause?
Where does the verb appear in a special conditional clause?

answers.answer: At the beginning of the clause
At the end of the clause

questions_and_answers.question: How is the sentence 'Wäre ich nicht Kandidat geworden, hätte ich grosse Schwierigkeiten gehabt' structured?

answers.answer: It begins with the verb followed by the subject

questions_and_answers.question: Can a special conditional clause appear before or after the main clause?

answers.answer: Yes, it can appear in either position
No, only before the main clause
No, only after the main clause
No, it must always appear at the end

questions_and_answers.question: Which language sometimes mirrors the German special conditional clause by inverting subject and verb?
What is one purpose of the special conditional clause?

answers.answer: It shortens conditional sentences by omitting the clause introducer
It changes the sentence to future tense

questions_and_answers.question: In the example sentence about the Eastern Zone, what would improve conditions?

answers.answer: If the conditions were better, there would be fewer refugees

questions_and_answers.question: What does the clause 'Man hätte ihn als politischen Flüchtling anerkannt' imply?

answers.answer: Recognition as a political refugee was possible if circumstances were different
Recognition is not related to circumstance
He was recognized as a citizen

questions_and_answers.question: Which element can appear twice in a conditional sentence when using the longer würde phrase?

answers.answer: It usually does not appear twice
It can appear only in the main clause
It can only appear in the conditional clause

questions_and_answers.question: Which of the following best paraphrases the special conditional clause concept?

answers.answer: A conditional clause without 'wenn' starting with the verb

articles.text:
THE SPECIAL CONDITIONAL CLAUSE
In place of the -clause in conditional sentences a SPECIAL CONDITIONAL CLAUSE may occur, in which the clause introducer is omitted and the clause begins with the finite, or inflected verb form followed by the subject:
Wäre ich nicht Kandidat geworden, hätte ich grosse Schwierigkeiten gehabt, meinen Betrieb zu halten.
oder
Wenn ich nicht Kandidat geworden wäre, hätte ich grosse Schwierigkeiten gehabt, meinen Betrieb zu halten.
Had I not become a probational party member it would have been difficult for me to keep my business going.
If I had not become a probational party member it would have been difficult for me to keep my business going.
The SPECIAL CONDITIONAL CLAUSE may occur in either position in the sentence. Here are additional examples:
Man hätte ihn als politischen Flüchtling anerkannt, wäre er nicht Funktionär der SED gewesen. oder Man hätte ihn als politischen Flüchtling anerkannt, wenn er nicht Funktionär der SED gewesen wäre.
He would have been recognized officially as a political refugee, had he not been an official of the SED.
He would have been recognized officially as a political refugee if he had not been an official of the SED.
Wären die Zustände in der Ostzone besser, würde es weniger Flüchtlinge geben. oder Wenn die Zustände in der Ostzone besser wären, würde es weniger Flüchtlinge geben.
If conditions in the Eastern Zone were better there would be fewer refugees.
Note that English, too, sometimes omits the clause introducer and inverts subject and verb in formal style. The construction is much more frequent in German however and is not limited to specifically formal situations.
